description: The CVEs CISA has added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, newest first, from EchelonGraph's copy of that catalog, which polls CISA's feed every 5 minutes. Each row in kev gives cve_id, kev_added_date (CISA's dateAdded), kev_due_date, kev_vendor, kev_product, kev_vuln_name and kev_ransomware (known ransomware-campaign use), EchelonGraph's severity, cvss_v3_score, epss_score, epss_percentile and eg_kev_tier for the CVE, and our_first_seen_kev, when EchelonGraph's poller first recorded the CVE entering the catalog (null where no such record exists). Filter by since and until (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, on kev_added_date), ransomware, and vendor (an exact, case-insensitive match on kev_vendor); page with limit (1 to 200, default 50) and cursor, passing back the previous page's next_cursor with the same filters. total counts the CVEs matching the filters; kev_listed_total counts every CVE EchelonGraph holds as KEV-listed, and catalog.catalog_count is CISA's own count in the catalog last fetched, so a gap between the two is entries not yet in EchelonGraph's CVE table, which no page returns. CISA's requiredAction, shortDescription and notes are not in these rows: each CVE's own record carries them, verbatim and labelled as CISA's. Its structured result's measured_at is our last successful fetch of CISA's feed (null when the API does not give it), coverage counts the CISA KEV catalog (total, returned, kev_listed_total, catalog_count, limit, has_more) and freshness gives last_successful_fetch_at, catalog_version and date_released. Past 30,000 characters of JSON, the first text block holds data cut to fit, and the note says what the cut leaves out and where to read it (TEXT CUT); data in the structured result always holds it whole. Cut, each row keeps fewer fields, cve_id, kev_added_date, kev_vendor and kev_ransomware at least, or rows are left out, and next_cursor still continues after the last row of the page, not of the text.

ransomware.description: true: only CVEs with known ransomware-campaign use; false: only those without

since.description: earliest kev_added_date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (an RFC 3339 timestamp is read as the date written in it, with the time and offset dropped; anything else is refused)

until.description: latest kev_added_date to include, YYYY-MM-DD (an RFC 3339 timestamp is read as the date written in it, with the time and offset dropped; anything else is refused)

vendor.description: CISA vendorProject, an exact case-insensitive match, e.g. 'Microsoft'

name: kev_recent

catalog_count.description: CISA's own count, in the catalog last fetched.

has_more.description: Whether next_cursor names a further page.

kev_listed_total.description: Every CVE EchelonGraph holds as KEV-listed.

coverage.description: What the answer covers; null where the answer says nothing about it.

kev.description: Newest kev_added_date first; rows within one date are ordered by cve_id.

our_first_seen_kev.description: When EchelonGraph's poller first recorded the CVE entering the catalog; null where no such record exists.

last_successful_fetch_at.description: When CISA last answered our poll of its feed: a 200 we applied, or a 304 Not Modified.

freshness.description: The producing radar's last completed check (last_run_at), where the API serves one.

measured_at.description: When the underlying observation was made, as the API states it; null when the answer does not say or holds no observation.

state.description: measured: a measurement of what was asked; an exposure count is measured only with measured_at and method. not_assessed: the answer holds no dated measurement of what was asked, so no count in it is presented as one; it can still relay a count, as what the source holds on record, undated, and its notes (and exposure_state, where the result carries it) say what each count is.

catalog_count.description: CISA's own count, in the catalog last fetched.

has_more.description: Whether next_cursor names a further page.

kev_listed_total.description: Every CVE EchelonGraph holds as KEV-listed.

kind.description: What failed: the request (network, timeout), the answer (http, not_json, not_object, unexpected_shape), the input, or this server.

message.description: The cause: the API's own message, or what went wrong.

path.description: The API path requested, when a request was made.

status.description: The HTTP status, when the API answered one.

state.description: failed: the lookup did not complete. invalid_input: the input was refused, so nothing was looked up. Neither is a finding.

title: Recent CISA KEV additions
